narration: Breaks into a run — covers ground.
effect: **Action.** Gain extra movement equal to base speed for this turn.

narration: Steps deliberately back — moves without provoking the swing.
effect: **Action.** Movement this turn doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

narration: Drops into a low, weaving stance — eyes everywhere at once.
effect: **Action.** Until start of next turn: attacks against this NPC have disadvantage (if NPC can see the attacker) AND this NPC has advantage on Dex saves. Lost if incapacitated or speed drops to 0. Apply `@dodging` to track.

narration: Lunges in and clamps onto the target — wraps arms / paws / coils.

roll.label: Athletics (grapple)
roll.notes: Athletics contest vs target's Athletics OR Acrobatics. On success: target is **grappled** (speed 0). Use `@grappled` on the target's tab to track. Escape is the target's action: another contest.

narration: Distracts the target or steadies the ally's grip.
effect: **Action.** Pick one ally within 5 ft. They gain **advantage** on their next attack roll OR ability check (target must be specified). Lasts until the start of this NPC's next turn.

narration: Slips behind cover — flattens against a surface, holds breath.

roll.label: Stealth
roll.notes: Compare to each unaware PC's passive Perception. PCs whose PP > result spot the NPC. Requires cover or distraction.

narration: Sets feet and shoves — leverages weight against the target.

roll.label: Athletics (push)
roll.notes: Athletics contest vs target's Athletics OR Acrobatics. On success: push target 5 ft. Pass `modifier` per-NPC at call time if Athletics > +0.

narration: Hooks a leg / drives downward — drops the target flat.

roll.label: Athletics (shove prone)
roll.notes: Athletics contest vs target's Athletics OR Acrobatics. On success: apply `@prone` to the target. Melee attackers gain advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage on hits.

prerequisite: PC within 60 ft just started casting a spell Aelric can see; uses Aelric's reaction
narration: He snaps his fingers — frost crackles in the air between his hand and the caster, and their magic shatters into glittering motes.

roll.label: Counterspell ability check
roll.notes: Auto-counters spells of level 3 or lower (Counterspell is cast at 3rd-level). For 4th-level+ spells, this roll must beat DC **10 + spell level** to negate. DM tracks reaction usage — Counterspell shares Aelric's one-per-round reaction slot with Shield.

trigger.match: any creature casts a spell within 60 ft

narration: Aelric whispers a single word; warmth spreads from his palm.
effect: Restore 2d8+3 HP to one ally within 30 ft. (use as bonus or main action; 3/day slots)

narration: Aelric extends a frost-rimed hand; a beam of pale cold lances out, leaving a trail of crystallizing air.
He sweeps both hands skyward — hailstones the size of fists rip down through a 20-ft cylinder of swirling cold.

prerequisite: free hand for somatic; not wearing armor
narration: He traces a sigil in the air around himself — a faint blue shimmer settles like a second skin.
effect: Aelric's AC becomes **15** for 8 hours (or until dispelled / another instance is cast on him). Usually already active when combat starts — only recast if dispelled.

prerequisite: Aelric must be conscious; uses one of 3 daily slots
narration: Mist coils around him for an instant — and then he's gone, reappearing 30 ft. away in a swirl of frost.
effect: **Bonus action.** Aelric teleports up to **30 ft.** to an unoccupied space he can see. Does not trigger opportunity attacks. (3/day — track uses; refresh on long rest.)

prerequisite: Aelric was hit by an attack or targeted by Magic Missile; uses Aelric's reaction
narration: A wall of invisible force flickers into being at the last instant, deflecting the blow.
effect: **Reaction.** +5 AC against the triggering attack (often turns a hit into a miss) AND until the start of Aelric's next turn. Also auto-negates Magic Missile. Shares reaction slot with Counterspell.

trigger.match: Aelric is hit by an attack (any range)

prerequisite: Once per day. He usually spends it in **round 2**, the round after the first man goes down — or before a river crossing, or a hill, or anything he has decided is difficult for them.
narration: He walks the line with a hand out, touching shoulders that are mostly not there, saying something over each of them too quietly to catch.
effect:
**Action, 1/day.** Ambrose casts *Bless* on up to **three** of his men within 30 ft. For **1 minute** (concentration — and he is a terrible concentrator; **[ASK PLAYER] any damage he takes, DC 10 or the higher of 10 / half the damage**, and he loses it), each blessed skeleton adds **1d4** to every attack roll and every saving throw.

At +4 to hit, a blessed skeleton is swinging at roughly **+6.5**. That is real, it is one action he is not spending on `On Your Feet`, and **it ends the moment somebody makes him lose concentration** — which is one more reason to go through him instead of around him.

He is not buffing troops. He thinks he is saying a blessing over tired men before a hard stretch of road, and he is right about the second half of that.

prerequisite: Fires the moment Ambrose is **reduced to 0 HP** (dead OR knocked out — nonlethal counts), **or** grappled / restrained / incapacitated / stunned / paralysed / held prone, **or** unable to speak (gagged, hand over the mouth, *Silence*, a successful *Command*, shoved face-down), **or** he calls the halt himself. No save. No DC. No DM discretion.
narration: "...Halt." Very quietly. And then, in the parade-ground voice, and it cracks: "COLUMN. HALT."
effect:
**THE CONTROLLER-BREAK. This is the mechanic the variant exists for — state it to the table as a rule, not a ruling.**

The skeletons here are **not independently animate**. They are following him. The instant the prerequisite above is met, then at the **start of the next skeleton's turn**, every remaining skeleton **stops where it stands, mid-swing.** Immediate, automatic, no roll. They stand still for one full round.

**Then, at the end of that round:**
- **He is still down or still stopped** → every skeleton turns west and reverts to **Shamble Onward**. v1 rules resume exactly: no attacks unless individually damaged, blocked, or grabbed; no pursuit. **The fight is over** unless the party restarts it.
- **He got free** → he can start them again, but it costs his **entire action** (`the_column_moves`). Every time.

**Make it findable.** He announces `On Your Feet` out loud, by name, every single time he uses it. He is telling the party how to beat him and he does not know that is what he is doing. A party that stands in the open trading swings loses slowly; a party that grabs the chaplain wins in two rounds. That is the lesson.

trigger.match: a skeleton of the procession within 30 ft drops to 0 HP

narration: He says the man's name. Then he says who is waiting for him, and where, and how far.
effect:
**Reaction, no roll, no mechanical effect — this is a voice tool and it is the best thing he does.** The first time one of his men goes down within 30 ft, Ambrose names him aloud: rank, company, home village, and the person expecting him. He is not accusing anybody. He is doing the only part of his job he has left.

**It is also the switch.** From his NEXT turn onward the party are deserters and grave-robbers, and `radiant_flame` comes off the shelf. Until this fires, he does not attack at all.

**If it is the skeleton wearing the corroded bronze pauldron — Corwin Caldor — use this, verbatim, and let it land:**

> "Corwin Caldor. Third company, Ridgeward. He has a wife at Ardenford — **Maris**. He talks about her. He talks about her the entire time, he does not *stop*." *(He is smiling.)* "I promised him I'd get him to the door."

The party were sent here by that man's grandson. Do not explain that to the table. They will get there.

**Once per round; refreshes at the start of his turn.** If you need more names for the other men, take them off the third company muster roll in his satchel: Serjeant Callow, Ostry, Penn, the Byrne boy who was seventeen.

prerequisite: **Last resort only.** He is cornered, out of range options, or something is inside his reach and he cannot back off. He is bad at this and he knows it, and he apologises while he swings.
narration: He gets the censer-head up and brings it down with both hands and an expression of genuine regret. "I'm sorry. I'm sorry — I did ask."

attacks.name: Censer Mace
attacks.rider_on_hit: The radiant is **him**, not the weapon — the mace is mundane loot. Ugly detail worth playing: this is the one thing on the field that puts his own men down for good (radiant destruction blocks `On Your Feet`). He has never once noticed.

prerequisite: One of his men dropped to 0 HP this fight, Ambrose can **see** it and **speak**, and that particular skeleton has not already been called back once. **Not usable** if it was destroyed by **radiant damage**, by a **critical hit**, or if a PC has **scattered its bones or laid them in a cairn** (one action, no check — tell the party this is possible the first time one of them looks at a cairn).
narration: "Serjeant. Serjeant, on your feet. We're not there yet."
effect:
**Action.** Ambrose calls a fallen man **by name** — out loud, every time, no exceptions. At the **start of that skeleton's next turn** it stands back up in its own space with **4 HP** and resumes acting normally.

**Hard caps, so this stays level-1-safe:**
- **3 uses** (one per skeleton in the default v3 roster; **4** if you're running the six-PC roster of four skeletons).
- **Each individual skeleton can be called back once, ever.** A man who goes down twice stays down.
- It comes back at **4 HP**, not full. It is a formality, not a heal.

**Saying the name out loud is not flavour — it is the tell.** This is how the party learns that the man in the cassock is the reason the fight will not end. He is handing them the solution and does not know it.

And then, to whoever put the man down, conversationally, the way you'd explain a rule to a child: *"You don't get to leave him here. His mother is four miles that way."*

prerequisite: **He does not attack anybody until a PC has put one of his men down.** Not if they draw steel, not if they block the road, not if they threaten him personally with a blade at his throat. Once somebody has dropped a skeleton, the party are **deserters and grave-robbers** and he is an officer with the authority to discipline them, and he is entirely calm about it. He targets whoever interfered with the march most recently — NOT the squishiest PC. He stays at range, behind his men, ideally on a cairn; at 11 HP he cannot afford a melee round.
narration: He raises two fingers, the way you would to bless somebody, and a hard clean light goes out of them.

prerequisite: A PC spends an **action** speaking the closing of the burial office over Ambrose. Any faith, any tradition, anyone with a holy symbol or a funeral in their memory. Requires the party to have first understood what he is — [ASK PLAYER] **DC 13 Religion or Insight** (free for anyone who simply watches him for a round).
narration: For one second he is not confused at all. "Oh. — I did lose them, didn't I."
effect:
**The non-violent solve. It is the good ending and it pays FULL encounter XP — say so out loud.**

This is not necromancy and never was. It is a **burial rite**, interrupted a hundred and twenty-seven years ago by the Calderon second wave, still running because nobody ever said the last third of the words. Ambrose is the officiant. The reason nothing on this field can rest is that by the time it was his turn, there was nobody left standing to say them over him.

[ASK PLAYER] **DC 15 Religion or History**, one action, spoken aloud.

**Success:** the procession ends. Every skeleton lies down where it stands, without drama, the way a man sits down after a long day. Ambrose says his last line — *"See them the rest of the way."* — and is not there any more. A cassock, a mace, and the third company muster roll on the stones.

**Failure:** nothing bad happens. He doesn't notice, doesn't take offence, doesn't retaliate, doesn't get a free attack. Try again next round, as many times as they like.

**There is NO Persuasion answer.** No DC makes him understand what he is. A natural 20 on Persuasion buys a kind, attentive, completely useless reply. The delusion holds because he could not survive it breaking, and something in him knows that.

narration: He walks backwards ahead of them so he can keep an eye on the column, counting heads that are not there, apologising for the delay.
effect:
**Default action, every round, until the party makes this a fight.** Ambrose moves west with his men at the column's pace, calls the cadence, checks on them by name, and tries to give the party jobs — water, a hand with the cart, directions to the ford. **He makes no attack and orders no attack.** While he is doing this, the skeletons run **v1 rules exactly**: Shamble Onward, no hostility, no pursuit, provoked only individually. The party has the whole scene to decide what this is.

**He never opens the fight.** Not if they draw, not if they block the road, not if they insult him. The first violence on this field is always the party's.

**This action is also how he restarts a broken column.** If the procession was broken (he was at 0 HP, grappled, restrained, incapacitated, held prone, or unable to speak) and he has since gotten free, restarting the march costs his **entire action** — no attack, no raise, nothing else, that turn. Grappling him twice is a legitimate strategy and it should cost him two full turns.

**Voice:** warm, brisk, unhurried, busy. He interrupts himself to check the column. He calls everyone "gentlemen" and doesn't notice. He is never cruel and never wrong about anything except the one fact at the centre of him: *the battle was three days ago, and the men are tired, not dead.*

trigger.match: any damage (uses reaction once per round)

narration: The shape blurs — the spirit slides through stone and flesh alike, repositioning beyond reach.
effect: Move up to 40 ft (or fly 40 ft hover) without provoking opportunity attacks. Can pass through walls/creatures. Takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

narration: The spirit lashes out — two ghostly claws rake through the air, leaving frost-mist trails.
The spirit splits its jaws — a piercing wail of layered voices ripples outward, scouring the mind.

prerequisite: **Nonlethal by default.** This is the same swing as the scimitar with a different thing on the end of it -- a cudgel, a boat-hook haft, a length of firewood. Damage that reduces a target to 0 HP with this action knocks them **unconscious and stable**, not dying. Nobody here wants a body.
narration: No blade. Just a swing that lands somewhere thick, with enough weight behind it to make a point.

attacks.name: Club
attacks.rider_on_hit: Nonlethal. If this drops the target to 0 HP they fall **unconscious and stable** -- no death saves.

prerequisite: Loaded. Reloading costs this bandit's whole next action if the DM is tracking it -- one shot, then it closes or it runs.
narration: A dry click, then the bolt. Crossbows are loud in enclosed places.

prerequisite: **Lethal.** Only drawn once this one has decided it is fighting for its life, or in a scene where nobody is pretending otherwise.
narration: The curved blade comes out low and fast, the way a man draws when he has done it in a hallway before.

prerequisite: This one is at or below half HP, **or** the leader is down, **or** half its side is down. It does not need permission -- each one breaks on its own.
narration: The weapon hits the ground before the hands go up. This was never worth dying over.
effect: The bandit drops its weapon, raises open hands, and stops being a combatant. It will **not** pick the weapon back up unless it is attacked again while surrendered -- do that and every other survivor on its side fights to the end instead of yielding. A surrendered bandit will: back away and leave; answer questions badly and evasively; and give up whatever it was carrying if pressed. It will not name the person who hired it unless the party has real leverage -- [ASK PLAYER] **DC 13 Intimidation or Persuasion** for a name. Killing a surrendered one is a choice the table gets to make out loud.

narration: The spider drives its fangs deep; venom pumps into the wound.
The spider rears and sprays a thick rope of webbing across the gap.
effect: One creature the spider can see within 60 ft: [ASK PLAYER] DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a fail, the target is Restrained until the web is destroyed (the web is an object: AC 10, HP 5, Vulnerable to fire, Immune to poison and psychic damage). Recharge 5-6 -- roll 1d6 at the start of the spider's turn; the web is available again on a 5 or 6.

narration: The wolf spider scuttles in fast, sinks its fangs, and skitters back.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.rider_on_hit: On a hit, the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save: [ASK PLAYER] -- 2d4 poison damage on a fail, half as much on a success.

narration: Hocks a glob of supercooled bile from a glacial gland in its throat.
Throws its head back and bellows a wave of stinging frost.
It lunges, raking with two crystalline claws and snapping its rime-fanged maw.

prerequisite: Stalker must move at least 20 ft. straight at the target this turn
pre_save: DC 15 Str save vs prone (target gets disadvantage on the bite to-hit if knocked prone — DM, apply if save fails)
narration: Coils, then explodes off the ice and slams shoulder-first.
Shards of ice erupt where the blow lands.

prerequisite: snowy or icy terrain
narration: Folds itself into a snowdrift; only the steam of its breath gives it away.

roll.label: Stealth
roll.notes: Compare result to each PC's passive Perception; PCs whose PP > result are fooled.

narration: Bowstrings sing. A volley of crude arrows hisses across the gap.
The pack swarms — claws rake and jaws snap in a frenzy of dust and snow.
The boss barks an order and lays in with the scimitar -- two swift, vicious cuts.

attacks.name: Scimitar 1
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage, add 1d4 slashing damage.

attacks.name: Scimitar 2
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage, add 1d4 slashing damage.

narration: The boss slips back through the rubble, shouting for cover.
effect: Bonus action: take the Disengage or Hide action. Available every turn.

trigger.match: the boss is hit by an attack while a goblin ally is within 5 ft

narration: The boss yanks a shrieking raider into the path of the blow and slips clear.
effect: When the boss is hit by an attack and a Small or Medium goblin ally is within 5 ft: the boss and that ally swap places, and the ally becomes the target -- apply the attack's damage to the raider, not the boss. One reaction per round.

narration: The boss snaps off two quick shots from the back of the warband.

attacks.name: Shortbow 1
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage, add 1d4 piercing damage.

attacks.name: Shortbow 2
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage, add 1d4 piercing damage.

narration: The goblin scrambles back over the rubble, quick and low.
effect: Bonus action: take the Disengage or Hide action. Available every turn — use it to kite behind boulder cover and stay hidden.

narration: The goblin darts in low and slashes with a notched scimitar.

attacks.name: Scimitar
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage (e.g. an ally within 5 ft of the target), add 1d4 slashing damage.

narration: The goblin looses an arrow from behind cover, then ducks back down.

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.rider_on_hit: If this attack had Advantage, add 1d4 piercing damage.

narration: Grek lays a hand on the wound; a precise warmth spreads, sealing torn flesh.
effect: Restore 1d8+3 HP to one ally Grek can touch. Once Grek has cast it, the slot is gone until long rest.

narration: Grek mutters and stamps a tinkered glyph; a mote of fire arcs from his palm.
Grek's shoulder-mounted Force Ballista whirs; a thrumming bolt of force lances out.
Grek mutters; a tiny gadget flickers — light, sound, recorded message, or pin-prick mark.
effect: Minor magic on a tiny object (one of: light, sound, recorded message, odor, identifying mark). Roleplay tool, not combat-action.

prerequisite: An ally gnoll within 5 ft just dropped to 0 HP; uses reaction (once per turn)
narration: Jorran tears into the fallen's flesh — the eating-rite, brief and sacred.
effect: **Reaction.** Gain 5 temporary HP AND advantage on the next attack roll before the end of Jorran's next turn. Mark this action USED via the right-click menu after firing.

narration: Jorran roars — fangs and raking claws lash out as one.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.rider_on_hit: If lunar (night) — DM, add +1d4 to the first attack this round

narration: Jorran swings the dwarf-forged pickaxe — the trophy of his first kill.
A sheath of magical frost rimes Maela's skin; her breath fogs.
effect: Cast at 2nd level: gain 10 temporary HP. While any temp HP remains, melee attackers take 10 cold damage on hit.

narration: Maela's eyes flash; twin beams of violet force lance out, one chasing the other.
Maela whispers her patron's name; a dark sigil shimmers above the target.
effect: Concentration, up to 1 hour. Pick a target + ability. Deal +1d6 necrotic on EACH of your attacks against that target. The target has disadvantage on chosen ability checks. Moves with target.

narration: Maela spreads her fingers; three jagged rays of fire arc from her hand.

prerequisite: An ally gnoll within 5 ft just dropped to 0 HP; uses reaction (once per turn)
narration: The matron lowers her head; the eating-rite is brief, ancient, sacred.
effect: **Reaction.** Gain 5 temporary HP AND advantage on the next attack roll before the end of the matron's next turn.

prerequisite: Once per day; concentration, 1 hour
narration: The matron touches the target — voices layer, then settle into the chosen one's bones.
effect: Pick an ally and an ability score. They gain advantage on ability checks of that score for 1 hour. (Str = also doubles carry; Con = +2d6 temp HP.) DM applies via the LLM or `note`.

prerequisite: Once per day (night-only); manually mark USED via the right-click chip menu
narration: A column of pale moonlight lances down where the matron points — flesh sears as it touches the beam.
The matron strikes — fangs and claws in a single, fluid motion.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.rider_on_hit: If lunar (night) — DM, add +1d4 to the first attack this round

narration: Pale fire blooms in the matron's palm; she flicks it at the target.

prerequisite: Once per day; ritual, 10 minutes
narration: The matron's voice deepens; the hyenas still, listening.
effect: **Roleplay only.** The matron can converse with beasts (including the valley hyenas) for 10 minutes. Use this if the party tries to negotiate with the pack.

narration: Orren explodes into motion — two more strikes inside one breath.
effect: Take one additional action this turn (typically another longsword_multiattack). Available once per short rest.

narration: Orren steps in low and high — a measured cut, then a second.
Orren plants his feet and steadies his breath — pain fades, briefly.
effect: Bonus action. Regain 1d10+4 HP. Available once per short rest.

prerequisite: A PC addresses the skeleton calmly instead of attacking it, and no attack has been made against it this round.
narration: The skull turns toward the voice and stops. Whatever is left in there is listening.
effect: The skeleton halts and orients on the speaker. [ASK PLAYER] DC 13 Persuasion **or** Religion check. **Success:** the skeletons are not hostile -- they are confused, and they are going *home*. They stand still while a calm voice keeps talking, and can be led, turned, or walked elsewhere. **Failure:** no harm done and no aggression triggered; the skeleton resumes Shamble Onward on its next turn and the party may try again. It understands the languages it knew in life but cannot speak and will not answer questions -- it responds to **tone**, not words.

narration: It walks. Empty sockets fixed west, it steps around the living the way a man steps around a fencepost.
effect: **Default action, every round, unless this skeleton has been damaged, blocked, or grabbed.** The skeleton moves its full 30 ft. west toward Ardenford and makes no attack. It steps *around* a creature standing in its path -- once. If a PC blocks it a second time, grabs it, or damages it, it counts as threatened and switches to Shortsword or Shortbow from its next turn on. A skeleton that is disengaged from does **not** pursue: it reorients west and resumes walking. No morale, no fear, no retreat -- once provoked it fights to 0 HP, and walks the rest of the time.

prerequisite: Provoked, but no reachable target -- the PC is on a cairn, a ledge, or across a gap. The skeleton will not climb or leave high ground to chase.
narration: It draws a warped bow with fingers that are more sinew than flesh, and looses.

prerequisite: This skeleton has been damaged, blocked, or grabbed -- an unprovoked skeleton uses Shamble Onward instead.
narration: The skeleton turns without hurry and drives a pitted shortsword forward, bone grinding on bone.

prerequisite: The stirge is **attached** to a creature. This happens automatically at the **start of the stirge's turn** and costs it nothing -- it is not an action, and there is no attack roll and no save.
narration: The body of it swells and darkens, and the person it is on can feel exactly what is being taken.

roll.label: Blood Drain (necrotic, automatic -- no attack roll, no save)
roll.notes: Applies at the start of each of the stirge's turns while attached. Two full turns of this on a level-1 PC is a real threat -- an unlucky level-1 wizard can be dropped by a creature worth 25 XP. Track which stirge is on whom.

prerequisite: Either the stirge has drained **twice** (it is gorged and done), **or** it has taken any damage at all while attached -- at 5 HP a stirge does not survive a second hit and it has no interest in finding out.
narration: It comes free with a wet sound, hangs heavy in the air for a beat, and climbs out of reach.
effect: The stirge spends **5 ft of its movement** to detach, then flies with the rest of its 40 ft **straight up** and out of melee reach -- moving away from an attached host this way does not provoke, but leaving a threatened space does, so use the ceiling. A **gorged** stirge (two drains) leaves the encounter entirely: it goes back to the roof-dark to digest and does not come down again. A **damaged** stirge circles at 20+ ft for a round, then picks a different target. Stirges have **no loyalty to each other and no morale to break** -- they are not a faction, they are weather. Killing them all is optional; the party can simply leave.

prerequisite: **Do not roll these into initiative at the top of the fight.** They come down mid-fight -- DM's call, but the good beat is the start of round 2 or 3, or the moment somebody shouts, or the first time a torch goes up. They were always there.
narration: The sound registers first and nobody can place it: a dry leathery flutter, directly overhead, getting closer.

roll.label: Stealth -- hanging in the roof-dark (Dex +3)
roll.notes: Compare to each PC's passive Perception. Beat it and the stirge's first Proboscis attack is made with **advantage** against a surprised target. This is one roll for the whole flight -- do not roll it per stirge.

effect: The stirges detach from the ceiling and drop. Roll initiative for them now and slot them into the existing order. Each picks the **nearest warm body** and goes for exposed skin -- neck, forearm, scalp. They have no interest in the fight anyone else is having and they do not care whose side anyone is on: a stirge will land on a smuggler as happily as on a paladin. **Flying 40 ft** with only **10 ft** on the ground: they stay off the floor, they cannot be flanked, and a PC who wants to hit one in the air had better have reach or a bow.

prerequisite: The stirge is **not already attached** -- an attached stirge cannot make this attack, it uses Blood Drain instead.
narration: It lands with almost no weight at all, and then something thin and hard goes straight in.

attacks.name: Proboscis
attacks.rider_on_hit: The stirge **attaches** to the target. While attached it makes no attacks, moves with the target, and drains **2d4 necrotic** at the start of each of its turns (see Blood Drain). It detaches itself with 5 ft of movement; the target or any creature within 5 ft can detach it by using an **action**. An attached stirge is still a legal target -- but AoE and misses spray the host.

prerequisite: Fires the moment the tough thinks the price has gone past the point of the job: it is at or below half HP, **or** two of its side are down, **or** a PC makes it a credible offer. The tough is the only one here who can end this for everybody, and it knows it.
narration: It puts a flat hand out sideways -- not at the party, at its own people. "That's it. That's enough."
effect: The tough stops fighting and starts talking, and its side stops with it. It is **not** begging: it names terms and it means them. Terms are always some version of *you get what you came for, we walk away breathing, nobody says a name to anybody.* If the party keeps swinging after this, the tough fights to 0 HP and so does everyone still standing -- the offer does not come twice. [ASK PLAYER] **DC 12 Persuasion or Intimidation** to close on the offered terms, or better; on a hard failure the tough takes the deal off the table and goes back to work. If the party accepts, the encounter is **over** -- award full XP.

prerequisite: Only when the tough is holding back from the line -- across water, from a boat, from the top of the stair. It will not stay at range once one of its own goes down.
narration: It braces the stock against a hip and takes the shot without hurrying, the way you shoot at something that cannot shoot back.

prerequisite: **Pack Tactics:** roll this attack with **advantage** if any ally of the tough is within 5 ft of the target and is not Incapacitated. Check the map before you roll -- with four of its people on the stairs this is advantage most rounds.
narration: It does not wind up. It just steps in and puts the mace where the target was about to be.

prerequisite: The target is **prone, grappled, restrained, or already at 0 HP**. This is not a fighting move -- it is what happens after the fighting. Damage is **nonlethal**: a target dropped by it is unconscious and stable, not dying. Roll with **advantage** (Pack Tactics or a helpless target -- either one gets you there).
narration: It gets a fistful of collar, and then it goes to work, unhurried, counting under its breath.

attacks.name: Pommel & Boot
attacks.rider_on_hit: Nonlethal. A target reduced to 0 HP by this is **unconscious and stable** -- no death saves, no maiming, and they will wake up in an hour hating everyone.

trigger.match: an ally of the tough within 15 ft drops to 0 HP

narration: It is moving before the body finishes falling.
effect: **Reaction.** The tough moves up to its full 30 ft toward the ally who just dropped and plants itself in the way, ending its move in the nearest space that puts its body between the fallen ally and whoever put them there. This movement does **not** provoke opportunity attacks. On its next turn it attacks that PC in preference to any other target, and its morale clock advances one step toward **Call It Off**. Once per round; refreshes at the start of its turn.

narration: The gnoll lunges — claws and fangs in a single sweep.

prerequisite: An ally gnoll within 5 ft just dropped to 0 HP; uses reaction (once per turn)
narration: She kneels to the fallen, jaws working — the eating-rite, swiftly done.
effect: **Reaction.** Gain 5 temporary HP AND advantage on the next attack roll before the end of the lieutenant's next turn.

narration: The lieutenant strikes — bite and claws in a tight, practiced combo.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.rider_on_hit: If lunar (night) — DM, add +1d4 to the first attack this round

narration: The hyena lunges in, jaws snapping.
Vessa moves — fast, low, gone before anyone tracks her.
effect: Bonus action. Choose: Dash, Disengage, or Hide. Available every turn.

narration: A muffled thwip — a quarrel jumps from Vessa's hand crossbow.
Vessa slips in close; her shortsword finds the gap between plates.

trigger.match: an attacker Vessa can see hits her with an attack

narration: Vessa twists at the last instant; the blow lands at half-force.
effect: Halve the damage from one incoming attack this round. Uses Vessa's reaction.

prerequisite: A PC tries a calm voice on it -- or the skeletons have already been talked down and someone assumes this one will follow.
narration: The head turns toward the voice. Something behind the face registers that a sound happened, and then it takes another step.
effect: **There is nothing in here to talk to.** Heed the Living does not work on the zombie -- no check, no DC, no partial success. Where a skeleton stops and listens to *tone*, this one has kept enough meat to rot and lost whatever the skeletons kept. It closes at its full **20 ft** and slams the nearest living thing. **This is the point of the variant:** a party that solves the battlefield with a gentle voice gets three skeletons standing quiet in a ring and one dead Calderon soldier still walking through the middle of them, and now they have to decide what to do about him while the others watch. No morale, no fear, no retreat, no pursuit beyond what it can reach at 20 ft.

prerequisite: Nearest living creature it can reach. No target priority, no flanking, no tactics -- it hits whatever is closest and keeps hitting it.
narration: The arm comes over in a slow, heavy arc, like a door closing on someone's hand.

prerequisite: Damage just reduced the zombie to **0 HP**. It does **not** get this save if the killing damage was **Radiant** or came from a **Critical Hit** -- in either of those cases it simply drops. DC = **5 + the damage taken from the killing blow** (the full damage rolled, not the amount that took it to 0).
narration: It goes down. Then a hand finds the ground, and the whole ruined weight of it starts levering back upright.

trigger.match: reduced to 0 HP by damage that is not radiant and not a critical hit

roll.label: Undead Fortitude (Con save, +3)
roll.notes: DC = 5 + damage taken. On a SUCCESS it drops to 1 HP instead of 0 and keeps acting. On a FAILURE it is finally down. Say the DC out loud before the roll -- the table needs to learn that big hits and radiant damage are the answer, and that chipping it for 3s can go on all night.

narration: Zor'gar's rage tips into frenzy — the world narrows to teeth and edge.
effect: Bonus action while raging: make one additional melee attack on each of your turns. After frenzy ends, gain 1 level of exhaustion.

narration: Zor'gar roars; the greataxe carves the air in a wide, brutal arc.
Zor'gar bares teeth, locks eyes — the rage rises, slow and inexorable.
effect: Bonus action. For up to 1 minute: advantage on Str checks/saves, +2 damage on Str-based melee, resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing. Ends if you don't attack or take damage for a turn.

narration: Zor'gar abandons his guard; every blow lands harder — and so does every one against him.
effect: Before the first attack on your turn: gain advantage on STR-based melee attack rolls this turn. Attacks against you have advantage until your next turn.
